description:
📝 Notes
Mar 5, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Amir Houieh provided updates on the analytics strategy for data segregation, confirmed the website is online with social media preview features in development, and presented an AI Studio prototype demonstrating Notion integration and content composition capabilities for writing blog posts. Noémi Biró shared a detailed prototype of Mycelium's attention recovery system, which includes scenarios for distraction intervention using box breathing and hyperfocus management by prompting necessary breaks. Gabor Kerekes reported an access issue with the AI Studio app, discussed the concept of attention as the central theme and economics of time, and described the stages of Mycelium's digestion of captured information using a new Mac OS capture tool, which aligns with Amir Houieh's implemented "learners."
Details
Discord Communication Concerns: Amir Houieh initiated the meeting by asking Noémi Biró about their use of Discord for receiving messages, as it is utilized as the team's shared workspace. Noémi Biró explained that they typically need to check Discord manually to see messages because they do not have the sound notifications turned on, and mentioned that they were in "focus mode" the previous day and did not check. Amir Houieh requested that Noémi Biró check Discord more regularly because it is where the team connects for work (00:00:00).
AI Studio App Access Issue: Gabor Kerekes reported an issue trying to access the AI Studio app, noting that it showed a "page not found" error despite attempting to log in with their correct account (00:00:00). They mentioned that they switched accounts, but the change did not seem to persist, which Amir Houieh found strange (00:02:15).
Analytics Strategy and Data Segregation: Amir Houieh presented an update on the analytics strategy, specifically detailing a new table designed to segregate data responsibilities between a Posthog integration and the internal database (DB). To minimize dependency and address privacy concerns, the suggestion is to primarily use the DB for calculating metrics whenever possible, reserving Posthog mainly for tracking user behaviors and user experience (00:03:32).
Website Updates and Social Media Previews: Amir Houieh confirmed that the website is now online and mentioned working on a social media preview feature that generates a thumbnail when a link is shared. The generated image includes elements like the domain type, which changes based on the shared content (e.g., 'blog' on 'body.io') (00:05:32).
AI Studio Prototyping - Notion Integration: Amir Houieh described an AI Studio prototype assuming integration with Notion, where Mycelium operates at the OS level and is accessible via a right-click menu (00:07:43). They showed a use case for writing a blog post, where Mycelium surfaces relevant content fragments and suggests potential topics and outlines (00:09:24).
Content Composition and Outline Generation: The Mycelium prototype demonstrated the capability to compose articles either by dragging and dropping content fragments into a Notion document or by generating and presenting three complete article outlines (00:09:24). Amir Houieh explained that the outlines show source connections, and users can insert the composed content directly into Notion if they are satisfied (00:10:35).
Attention Interruption Use Case Scenario: Noémi Biró shared a scenario prototype focused on attention recovery, particularly relevant for people with ADHD (00:13:43). The system, Mycelium, pulls the user's daily plan from Notion and displays a morning pop-up with the daily goal, timing, and focus mode status (00:14:54).
Scenario 1: Distraction and Intervention: Noémi Biró elaborated on a distraction scenario where the system detects the user getting sidetracked by unrelated content, such as a sewing tutorial. The intervention proposed is an OS-level overlay that initiates a 32-second box breathing exercise to help the user recover their focus (00:16:14).
Scenario 2: Hyperfocus and Break Management: A second scenario was mapped out for hyperfocus, where the system monitors time tracking data (like t-metric) and detects continuous work exceeding typical focus cycles (e.g., 3 hours and 41 minutes). The system intervenes to prompt a break, noting that cognitive performance tends to decline after three hours (00:17:19).
Remaining Attention Scenarios: Noémi Biró outlined two additional scenarios: one for when a person is "super scattered" (frequent context switching), and another for the end of a long day, where Mycelium uses data (like from an Aura ring) to determine low readiness and urges the person to wrap up their work. The discussion confirmed that Noémi Biró's focus was on activity logs, attention span, and the content context (00:18:40).
Mycelium as a Utility Layer/Ecosystem: The group discussed the potential for Mycelium to function as a core system supporting a utility layer or ecosystem, similar to Raycast, where users could develop their own utilities or plugins (00:19:50). The idea aligns with the metaphor of Mycelium as the underlying system, with use cases (the "mushrooms") popping up to the surface (00:21:53).
The Central Theme of Attention and Economics of Time: Gabor Kerekes identified attention as the central theme, focusing on developing a system that guides, stewards, and protects attention (00:23:14). They introduced the concept of framing one's life in terms of economics, where scarce resources like attention and time are considered a limited budget for investment (00:25:01).
Prototype Experimentation and User Interviews: Noémi Biró intends to make their attention scenario function using the t-metric API and test it for a few days (00:17:19) (00:33:15). Amir Houieh suggested involving a person they know with severe ADHD for interviews to gather user feedback. The group agreed that speaking to users and the audience is beneficial (00:31:10).
Defining Core Scenario Pillars: Amir Houieh identified two concrete foundational pillars based on the prototypes: "context isolation" or "context overwhelming," and "time tax" or "attention tax". They suggested continuing to build more use cases until the following week (00:34:23).
Mac OS Capture Tool and Mycelium Digestion: Gabor Kerekes reported building a capture tool that lives at the Mac OS level and is currently allowing Mycelium to digest captured information (00:35:57). Gabor Kerekes outlined the conceptual stages of this digestion process: accretion (floating information), nucleation (crystallization into threads from density), and absorption (threads exerting gravity) (00:38:15).
Overlap in Learning Mechanisms: Amir Houieh noted that the concepts of Mycelium thread formation (ingestion, observation, synthesizing) described by Gabor Kerekes align closely with how their implemented "learners" function, indicating a shared foundational logic (00:42:15). Gabor Kerekes expressed interest in experimenting with the "brain" component and connecting it to their work (00:43:17).
New Mac OS Sandbox Setup: Gabor Kerekes presented an update on a new sandboxing solution for the virtual machine, which uses a simplified script and leverages Mac OS's built-in virtualization support for better integration and optimization (00:44:23). The new setup is expected to speed up development by requiring less "babysitting" (00:47:17).
Focus for the Remainder of the Week: Amir Houieh confirmed that they will focus on Mycelium and the brain component for the rest of the day, with plans for a meeting with Noémi Biró for Civil the following day. Gabor Kerekes expressed a desire to try using the new sandbox to set up analytics repositories using agents as an exploration effort (00:48:37).
Suggested next steps
Amir Houieh will focus on Mycelium and Brain today to continue building, specifically by making a scenario with brain relevant to mycelium with some UI to evaluate it.
Noémi Biró will make the attention interrupt use case prototype function with the T-metric application and work on the second scenario related to the cycle.
Gabor Kerekes will figure out access for the song capture tool for capturing raising dots and share the script for the virtualization setup that uses the Mac OS built-in support for virtualization.
